content_text: [1/2 @gregoryblotnick] great intvw question for L/S would be: >wait for them to pitch whatever ("XYZ is a long because...") >ask basic questions, nothing too strenuous, poke holes in pitch >then, when they're finished, you say: "okay...now pitch it to me as a short." tests much more than just knowledge of #'s, especially if they don't see it coming you get to see their mental flexibility, objectivity, their command of all the emotional and cognitive biases that get in the way of every investor for L/S especially, you get trained to be fully direction-agnostic, so someone experienced is already coming in with the mindset of: "at $150 I'm neutral because it's fairly valued, at $100 r/r skews long, at $200 r/r skews short." takes a long time to unwire and rewire your brain this way, but someone who nails the question without missing a beat, they have the mindset to succeed in any sector coverage model. --- [2/2 @gregoryblotnick] can combine the above into 1-3 terms ("lack of mental rigidity", "objectivity," "freedom from preconcieved notions/biases") and add to this list... less obvious traits ex ante, but ones that really stand out when u see them displayed in an individual. https://x.com/gregoryblotnick/status/2045265997901545953?s=20
